settings.advanced.burst_decode_hint: Process tokens in batches internally for faster generation. Higher levels run faster but stream in larger chunks; lower levels stream more smoothly. Applies instantly, no restart.
settings.advanced.preserve_mid_system_ca: Preserve Prefix Cache for Mid-Conversation System Notes

When a model's chat template cannot render system or developer messages after the first turn, oMLX rewrites safe trailing notes into the nearest user message so long conversation history can remain prefix-cacheable. Tool call and tool result sequences are left unchanged.
settings.advanced.initial_cache_blocks_h: Blocks pre-allocated at startup. Higher values reduce dynamic allocation overhead.
settings.advanced.hot_cache_write_throug: Keep blocks in RAM AND write them to SSD immediately. Old sessions survive restarts and crashes; recent sessions resume at RAM speed.
settings.advanced.ane_compile_cache_hint: Keep the ANE programs macOS compiles for Qwen prefill so later loads reuse them instead of compiling again. Cuts repeat load time; macOS stores the artifacts in its own cache. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.advanced.gdn_cache_policy_hint: Some models use Gated DeltaNet (GDN) recurrent layers whose state cannot be reconstructed from KV cache blocks alone. An extra state snapshot lets oMLX resume cached prompts without recomputing them.
settings.advanced.gdn_snapshot_storage_h: Auto uses separate SSD files when SSD cache is enabled; otherwise it stores snapshots with the KV cache. With KV Cache follows the same RAM or SSD tier as KV blocks. Enable Hot Cache Only to keep it in RAM.
settings.advanced.gdn_pending_write_limi: Maximum RAM used by encoded snapshots waiting to be written to SSD. When the buffer is full, cache writes pause until space is available.
settings.advanced.gdn_sidecar_state_prec: Controls GDN state stored in SSD sidecars only. FP32 is the exact default. Reduced-precision modes use less space but introduce reconstruction error. Restored state always runs in FP32.
Reduced-precision GDN cache storage can change greedy outputs, break bit-level reproducibility, and reduce output quality. Use FP32 unless you explicitly accept this trade-off.
settings.advanced.max_audio_upload_size_: Maximum file size accepted by audio transcription and processing endpoints. Higher values can increase memory use for concurrent requests.
settings.advanced.sse_keepalive_mode_hin: How streaming HTTP connections stay alive during long prefills. 'Chunk' is most compatible (default). Switch to 'Comment' for the legacy ': keep-alive' format, or 'Off' to disable.

modal.model_settings.qwen4_ple_ssd_offlo: Keep the large PLE N-gram table on SSD and read only the required rows. This saves memory but can slow prefill after context changes.
Required because resident loading exceeds the configured model-memory limit.
modal.model_settings.deepseek_v41_ced_pr: Improves prefill speed by approximately 74–79% in tested configurations. Long-context accuracy is still being evaluated. Uses the model’s Causal Encoder–Decoder architecture to reduce decoder prefill computation.
modal.model_settings.deepseek_v41_engram: Keep Engram tables on SSD and prefetch required rows. Saves memory; speed depends on SSD reads. Changing this setting reloads the model.
Required because resident loading exceeds the configured model-memory limit.
modal.model_settings.thinking_budget_hin: Limit thinking tokens for reasoning models. Forces end of thinking when exceeded.
modal.model_settings.guided_grammar_hint: Apply an EBNF grammar by default for this model.
modal.model_settings.limit_tool_result_h: Truncate large tool results (e.g. file reads) to a token limit
modal.model_settings.turboquant_kv_hint: Compress KV cache using vector quantization. Lower bits = more compression, higher bits = better quality. Supports 2 to 8 bits.
modal.model_settings.k2_ane_hint: Use ANE for K2 prompt processing, including MoVA. Decode stays on GPU. ANE uses private Apple interfaces. Outputs may differ.
modal.model_settings.k2_ane_tune_hint: Optional tuning for long-prompt processing with MLP weights at eight bits or below. Results do not predict batching performance. Targets three minutes; loading and cleanup can take longer. You can enable ANE without testing.

modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_dual_hint: Pin one resident program to each physical ANE instance.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_gdn_hint: Also split eligible GDN input projections across the ANEs and GPU.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_cpu_hint: Requires a separate Qwen q4 checkpoint clone with floating tensors converted to FP16. Retune the MLP ANE share when enabled.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_cpu_schedu: Uses Apple's shared-resource scheduler hint and falls back automatically when unsupported. Eight workers is the measured starting point.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_tune_hint: Calibrate ANE, CPU, and GPU work on real model layers, then verify the predicted split end to end. Settings change only when you apply the result.
modal.model_settings.qwen_oq_a8_hint: Experimental GPU INT8 activation quantization for supported Q4/Q5 prefill operations. Requires M5-series or newer and the native kernels. Outputs and model quality may change; some quantization formats receive no acceleration. Cannot be combined with ANE prefill. Applies after the model reloads.
modal.model_settings.moe_expert_offload_: Stream Mixture-of-Experts weights from the checkpoint on demand, keeping only a fraction resident. Fits MoE models larger than memory; costs decode speed. Requires reload.
Cannot be combined with Lightning MTP, VLM MTP, or DFlash.
modal.model_settings.lightning_mtp_hint: Drafts several tokens per step with the model's built-in MTP head. Up to ~1.5x faster decoding. (Qwen 3.5/3.6, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.2)

modal.model_settings.vlm_mtp_processor_c: Unset repetition / presence penalty and guided grammar first — VLM MTP cannot apply these per-request logits processors. Thinking budget is supported.

models.oq.about_architecture_rules_body: keep MoE routers in fp16, protect shared experts and output-critical tensors, leave vision/audio encoders unquantized, and preserve SSM state tensors.
models.oq.about_layer_sensitivity_body: is measured with calibration prompts by comparing quantized-layer output error against the float baseline.
models.oq.about_mixed_body: The quantizer streams tensors from safetensors, measures layer sensitivity, and writes a byte-budgeted mixed-precision checkpoint. Standard oQ focuses on layer-level sensitivity and model-aware protection rules. oQe keeps that same oQ plan and adds imatrix-weighted affine quantization.
models.oq.about_mixed_heading: oQ and oQe: MLX-native mixed precision
models.oq.about_mixed_precision_body: allocates higher bits to sensitive layers and protected tensors while keeping the target bits-per-weight budget under a hard cap.
models.oq.about_oqe_body: oQe uses the same oQ sensitivity planner, then adds an importance-matrix calibration step. This is explicitly borrowed from the llama.cpp imatrix idea: collect activation energy from representative prompts, then use that information so quantization spends less error on the input channels that matter most.
models.oq.about_quote_1: Quantization should not be exclusive to any particular inference server.
models.oq.about_quote_2: oQ produces standard mlx-lm models that work everywhere — oMLX, mlx-lm, LM Studio, and any app that supports MLX safetensors format.
models.oq.about_step1_body: oQe runs calibration samples through the model and records average input activation squared, E[x^2], for each quantized Linear input channel.
models.oq.about_step2_body: For MoE SwitchLinear layers, oQe records one importance vector per expert using the router-selected expert indices, so inactive or rarely active experts are visible in the coverage report.
models.oq.about_step3_body: Calibration starts from the requested sample count and can continue up to the adaptive maximum when MoE expert coverage is not sufficient.
models.oq.about_step4_body: During affine quantization, oQe chooses scale/bias candidates by minimizing sum(importance * (weight - dequantized_weight)^2), not plain unweighted MSE.
models.oq.about_strict_note: If a tensor has no matching imatrix entry, the default behavior is to fall back to standard oQ for that tensor. Enable strict coverage to fail instead.
models.oq.about_subtitle: Compare standard oQ with oQe imatrix and how enhanced quantization works.
models.oq.about_table_oq_use: Fast, deterministic conversion with strong baseline quality
models.oq.about_table_oqe_use: Better low-bit retention, especially for MoE and activation-skewed layers
models.oq.sensitivity_model_hint: Use a quantized version of the source model to analyze layer sensitivity with ~4x less memory.
models.oq.text_only_hint: Excludes vision encoder weights. Output is a text-only model (~2-3% smaller).

bench.metrics.ttft.name: TTFT
bench.metrics.test.tooltip: Test case label in the format ppN/tgM. 'pp' = prompt processing (number of input tokens), 'tg' = token generation (number of output tokens). For example, pp1024/tg256 means 1024 input tokens and 256 output tokens.
bench.metrics.ttft.tooltip: Time to First Token — how long the user waits before seeing any output. The model must read and process the entire prompt (prefill phase) before generating the first token. Longer prompts = higher TTFT. Measured in milliseconds. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tpot.tooltip: Time Per Output Token — average interval between consecutive output tokens during the generation (decode) phase. Directly affects how fast text appears on screen. For example, 20ms/tok means ~50 tokens per second. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tg_tps.tooltip: Token Generation TPS — number of output tokens produced per second during the decode phase. This is the inverse of TPOT (e.g., TPOT 20ms = 50 tg TPS). The primary measure of how fast the model writes its response. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.pp_tps.tooltip: Prompt Processing TPS — how many input tokens the model processes per second during the prefill phase. Higher values mean the model reads your prompt faster, which directly reduces TTFT. Important for long-context workloads. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.e2e.tooltip: End-to-End Latency — total wall-clock time from sending the request to receiving the complete response. Equals TTFT + (TPOT x number of output tokens). This is the overall time the user waits for a full answer.
bench.metrics.throughput.tooltip: Total Throughput — combined input and output tokens processed per second. Shows overall system utilization including both prefill and generation. Useful for comparing total compute efficiency across different prompt lengths.
bench.metrics.peak_mem.tooltip: Peak GPU Memory — maximum GPU (unified) memory used during inference for this test case. Includes model weights, KV cache, and intermediate activations. Helps estimate how large a model your hardware can handle.
bench.metrics.batch_size.tooltip: Batch Size — number of requests processed simultaneously. Batching lets the GPU handle multiple requests at once, increasing total throughput but adding some latency per individual request. A 2x batch doesn't mean 2x speed due to memory bandwidth limits.
bench.metrics.speedup.tooltip: Speedup — how much faster token generation is compared to a single request (1x baseline). For example, 1.8x means batching produces tokens 1.8 times faster overall. Values above 1x show more efficient GPU utilization through batching.
bench.metrics.pp_tps_req.tooltip: Per-Request Prompt Processing TPS — the pp TPS divided by the batch size. Shows how fast each individual request's prompt is processed when sharing the GPU with other requests. Expect this to be lower than the single-request pp TPS since compute is shared.
bench.metrics.avg_ttft.tooltip: Average Time to First Token across all requests in the batch. Higher than single-request TTFT because the GPU must process multiple prompts. Shows the typical wait time each user experiences under batched workloads.
bench.metrics.ttft.description: Latency until the model starts responding. Measures prompt processing (prefill) speed. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tpot.name: TPOT
bench.metrics.tpot.description: Average time between each generated token. Measures decode speed. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tg_tps.name: tg TPS
bench.metrics.tg_tps.description: Output tokens generated per second. Inverse of TPOT. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.pp_tps.name: pp TPS
bench.metrics.pp_tps.description: Input/prompt tokens processed per second during prefill. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.e2e.name: E2E Latency
bench.metrics.e2e.description: Total time from request submission to complete response. Includes prefill + generation.
bench.metrics.throughput.name: Total Throughput
bench.metrics.throughput.description: Overall tokens (input + output) per second. Measures total system utilization.
bench.metrics.batch_size.name: Batch Size
bench.metrics.batch_size.description: Number of concurrent requests processed together. Higher batch sizes improve total throughput but increase per-request latency.
bench.metrics.speedup.name: Speedup
bench.metrics.speedup.description: Token generation throughput multiplier compared to single-request baseline (1x). Higher is better.
bench.metrics.pp_tps_req.name: pp TPS/req
bench.metrics.pp_tps_req.description: Prompt processing throughput divided by batch size. Shows per-request prefill speed under batching load.
